unruled:f8960.unsupported.reason: No defect. BUG-0408's additions (life insurance contract gain or loss, the capital loss carryforward adjustment) drew no finding and closed group 8's two lows. Findings 0 to 3 and 7 covered by siblings as in group 8; finding 4 is a model error; WIDE accepted.

findings.evidence: i8960 pp. 13-14. f8960.refund asks about any recovery or refund of an amount deducted on an earlier Form 8960 (naming a state income tax refund) and gates the same lines. As group 8 finding 0.
i8960 p. 13. Form 8814: scope.other_line16 ('filing Form 8814 (even with no tax)') refuses the return. As group 8 finding 1.
i8960 p. 13. Substitute interest and dividend payments and notional principal contract payments are Schedule 1 line 8z kinds refused by oi8z and s1.line8_other. As group 8 finding 1.
i8960 p. 13. A casualty or theft loss is refused by sa.unsupported. As group 8 finding 2.

i8960 p. 7, Line 2. f8960.line2 copies Form 1040 line 3b; Alaska Permanent Fund dividends are Schedule 1 line 8g (s1.line8g), not in line 3b, so line 2 never includes them and no line 7 modification is needed.
i8960 p. 7: qualified-plan annuities draw Yes though line 3 is zero. Safe; as group 8 finding 5.
i8960 pp. 7, 22: Form 8815 draws Yes though line 1 and MAGI are right. Safe; as group 8 finding 6.
i8960 p. 13. A Schedule K-1 (Form 1041) is refused by scope.schedule1 ('estates or trusts ... Schedule K-1'); other pass-through income is named here. As group 8 finding 4.

unruled:gift.special.reason: No defect. Both findings WIDE (accepted); PENDING-4-5 (publicly traded undefined) closed by credits-misc PENDING-4, whose definition matches i8283 p. 9 and does not narrow the exception.

findings.evidence: i8283 pp. 1, 3: Section B turns on the deduction after reductions; property worth over $5,000 with a reduced deduction of $5,000 or less is refused though the helper computes it. Safe (as round 1).
i8283 pp. 3, 9: vehicles reportable in Section A (deduction $5,000 or less, or limited to gross proceeds with a CWA) are refused. Safe; as group 4 finding 2.

unruled:person.x_other.reason: BUG-0292 is fixed (BUG-0313): the earlier-year HSA excess is asked whether or not a 2025 Form 8889 exists, and whether or not it was ever reported. The remaining findings are accepted over-refusals.

findings.evidence: An ABLE excess returned in time answers Yes: a harmless over-refusal.
An excess resolved before 2025 answers Yes: a harmless over-refusal.
An RMD deadline outside 2025 answers Yes: a harmless over-refusal.
An HSA excess eliminated during 2025 answers Yes: an accepted over-refusal, since lines 42 to 46 are not computed.
An IRA excess absorbed in 2025 answers Yes: a harmless over-refusal.
Either answer is safe in the direction that matters; Yes refuses. Same over-broad wording.

unruled:refund.not_2024.reason: No defect. One WIDE (non-itemizer refused though line 1 is zero), as group 4 finding 2. PENDING-4-7 (2024 tax paid before 2024) closed by credits-misc PENDING-5; the screen widened only.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 88; p525 p. 24: a 2024 non-itemizer or sales-tax elector who paid part of 2024 tax in 2025 answers Yes and is refused though the taxable refund is zero. Safe; as group 4 finding 2.

unruled:retirement.special.reason: No defect. Round 3's additions (nonperiodic payments on or after the annuity starting date that are a single sum at the start, fully discharge the contract or reduce later payments; a recontribution of a wrongfully levied distribution) drew no finding. Findings 0, 1 and 4 repeat groups 9 and 10; finding 2 is finding 1's pre-1987 variant; finding 3 can only refuse.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 27, Exception 2. retirement.bad_code refuses a roth_ira account with any code other than qualified_roth_Q and gates the same lines. As groups 9 and 10, finding 0.

p575 p. 17; i1099r pp. 13, 15. Box 5 is subtracted: retirement.plan_excluded is box 5 plus the amount rolled over, and retirement.plan_simple subtracts it for any plan distribution, periodic or not. Box 5 is the cost 'that the employee may recover tax free this year', which the payer figures (by the pro-rata rule for a distribution before the annuity starting date). As groups 9 and 10, finding 1.
p575 p. 17; i1099r p. 15. As finding 1: the cost-first recovery of pre-1987 contributions is part of the tax-free amount the payer reports in box 5, which retirement.plan_simple subtracts.
p575 p. 23. A plan loan offset with no basis and no rollover is refused though the tool would compute it; refusal only.
i1040gi p. 27, Exception 1. A pension or qualified Roth filer with nondeductible traditional IRA basis may answer Yes and be refused; refusal only. As groups 9 and 10, finding 2.

unruled:s1.alimony_unsupported.reason: Defect: payments under a decree of divorce or separate maintenance while the spouses are members of the same household are not alimony, and neither the screen nor the amount questions say so (PENDING-7-3, medium, rare). PENDING-4-8 (part continuing after death) closed by income PENDING-1, a widening. Community income, noncash and property items and the post-2018 modification are covered by s1.alimony, s1.alimony_received and s1.alimony_paid; the WIDE findings are accepted.

findings.evidence: p504 p. 13. s1.alimony_received and s1.alimony_paid say 'cash payments only, so do not include ... your own part [your spouse's part] of community income', the amounts copied into s1.alimony_refused and s1.paid_refused (BUG-0240). As group 4 finding 1.
p504 p. 13. The same amount questions exclude 'noncash property settlements ... or payments to keep up or the use of the payer's property'. As group 4 finding 1.

p504 p. 14: 'Payments to your spouse while you're members of the same household aren't alimony if you're legally separated under a decree of divorce or separate maintenance. A home you formerly shared is considered one household'. Not in the screen nor in s1.alimony_received/paid; a payer still sharing the home under a decree enters the payments and deducts them on line 19a. PENDING-7-3, medium (rare).
p504 p. 13, Example 2: home owned only by the recipient is fully alimony but answers Yes. Safe; as group 4 finding 3.
p504 p. 16: a decrease with no recapture is refused. Safe; as group 4 finding 4.

p504 p. 16, Example 2. After income PENDING-3, s1.alimony counts 'only payments made before any change after 2018 that expressly applies the post-2018 rules', and s1.alimony_received/paid exclude 'payments made after the agreement was changed after 2018' in that way; the January to May payments are the ones entered.

unruled:s1.cod_unsupported.reason: Round-1 PENDING-2-3 closed (any other amount deductible if paid); the short-sale finding is covered (p4681's own short-sale example uses the canceled amount, and the property sale is refused by scope.other_income); the rest WIDE.

findings.evidence: p4681 pp. 4, 10; forms/2025/scope.yaml: p4681 p. 10, Example 3 (short sale): the lender cancels 'the remaining $115,000 of the outstanding $735,000 debt' and that $115,000 is the canceled debt: the Form 1099-C box 2 amount the tool enters. The gain or loss on selling the property is not a supported securities sale, so scope.other_income ('other income ... outside ... supported securities sales') refuses.
p525 p. 20: The 'would have been deductible' qualifier read as also covering box 3 interest: a filer with nondeductible interest answers yes and is refused (safe); the other reading is correct.
p4681 p. 4: Taxable nonbusiness student loan: refused. Safe.
p4681 p. 3: Nonrecourse discount with collateral kept: refused though computable. Safe.

unruled:s1.uc_unsupported.reason: No defect. Three WIDE (accepted, as group 4); PENDING-4-9 closed by income PENDING-2, a widening. The paystub-label UNCLEAR is presentation: the question follows the i1040gi wording and the ambiguity is in the filer's records (low).

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 89: a repayment of $3,000 or less of earlier-year compensation is refused though line 7 is unaffected. Safe; as group 4 finding 1.
i1040gi p. 89: contributions with no 2025 compensation. The screen is asked under s1.has_uc, and line 7 is zero either way. Safe; as group 4 finding 0.
i1040gi p. 89: earlier-year contributions already recovered draw Yes; refused though computable. Safe.

i1040gi p. 89 Caution and TIP: the question names unemployment contributions and excludes paid family leave and disability contributions, as the source does. A combined paystub label is a records question no rewording resolves; the cost of a wrong No is line 7 not reduced by the contribution. Low.

unruled:sales.special.reason: No defect. The allowed-or-allowable wording (BUG-0418) closed the NARROW finding of the previous rerun (a home whose depreciation was allowable but never claimed); the WIDE finding is accepted as in group 8.

findings.evidence: i1040sd p. 12, Line 19. An S corporation or trust interest whose entity holds only section 1250 property is refused though no line 19 look-through entry results. Safe; as group 8 finding 0.

unruled:sb.line8.reason: Round-1 PENDING-2-5 closed (loans count; a trust that existed at any time during 2025); the grantor-trust owner is outside the line 8 question and the gated lines; WIDE accepted.

findings.evidence: i1040sb p. 3; f1040sb line 8; forms/2025/sb.yaml: Schedule B line 8 asks only about a distribution, a grantor or a transferor. The p. 3 sentence on owners under the grantor trust rules concerns the trust's Form 3520-A, not this return. The gated lines (sb.line2, line3, line6) do not change, and the printed No answers the form's question.
i1040sb p. 3: A loan outside the 'generally' rule draws yes: refused. Safe (widening from BUG-0246).
i1040sb p. 3: Grantor or transferor with no Form 3520 requirement: refused; lines unaffected. Safe.

i1040sb p. 3: Transfer before 2025 to a trust still in existence: the clause 'a foreign trust that existed at any time during 2025' points to yes. A reading that keeps the opening 'During 2025' for the grantor limb prints No on line 8, and lines 2, 3 and 6 are unaffected. The residual comes from the form's own line 8 wording. No action needed.

unruled:scope.other_line16.reason: One low defect in wording R0 kept unchanged (BUG-0433, the Form 8615 condition omits the IRS examples of unearned income); the CFC/PFIC findings are the accepted over-refusal; 965(i) falls under the opening clause.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 36. As the prior ruling (finding 3): a triggered section 965(i) liability is an 'additional Form 1040 line 16 tax' under the question's opening clause, which the list only illustrates. Rare.
i8960 p. 22; i1040gi p. 34. Any CFC or PFIC stock, and Form 8621, is refused even with no line 16 tax (BUG-0409, accepted over-refusal). Safe.

i1040gi p. 36: 'more than $2,700 of unearned income (such as taxable interest, ordinary dividends, or capital gains (including capital gain distributions))'. The question gives the threshold without the examples, so a child with mostly capital gains may answer No and Form 8615 tax is missed. The words are the prior wording's (R0 changed none); BUG-0433, low.

unruled:scope.schedule1.reason: No defect, after the second round: the first round's UNCLEAR on alimony paid came from R0 sorting 'alimony under an agreement made before 2019' under income, which narrowed it to alimony received (s1.alimony asks received or paid); the list was restored to the original order and the review rerun, which raised no such finding. The NARROW findings are covered by other gates; the WIDE and UNCLEAR ones can only refuse.

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 40: a passive Schedule C answers sc.passive No and is refused (sc.screened refuses sc.line1), and scope.other_income asks 'income or loss from a passive activity'. As the prior ruling (finding 0).
i1040gi p. 104: s1.sc_1a (from sc.tips_ot) refuses s1a.line5_calc for qualified tips received in a trade or business. As the prior ruling (finding 1).
i1040gi p. 108: s1.sc_1a (from sc.tips_ot) refuses s1a.line14b_calc for overtime on Form 1099-NEC or 1099-MISC. As the prior ruling (finding 2).
i1040sc p. 5, Line 1, Statutory employees: a statutory employee's Schedule C answers sc.statutory Yes and is refused (sc.screened); either reading of this question refuses.
i1040gi p. 42; i1040sse p. 1: church wages under $108.28 are refused though line 1z is right. Safe; as the prior ruling (finding 3).

i1040gi p. 40, Step 2 question 4. A Yes refuses; a No leaves a business rental of personal property on Schedule C, where a rental activity answers sc.passive No and sc.screened refuses it. Either answer refuses or computes correctly.

unruled:ssb.terror_disability.reason: Round-1 PENDING-3-4 closed ('eligible for coverage ... whether or not you made a claim'); the full-retirement-age finding remains WIDE (T-008).

findings.evidence: i1040gi p. 31: Benefits after full retirement age read as disability payments: yes refuses what the tool computes. Safe (T-008, round 1).

unruled:refund.box8.reason: No defect: the UNCLEAR reading errs only toward YES (refusal of a refund the tool computes), and the nontaxable business-tax refund is refused; both accepted WIDE.

findings.evidence: f1099g p. 5 Box 8: 'an income tax that applies exclusively to income from a trade or business and is not a tax of general application'. The misreading the model describes (a general income tax that in the filer's case reached only business income) yields YES and a refusal (eval: stage16.mut.refund_single_unasked with refund.box8 yes -> refund.taxable, s1.line1, f1040.line11a, f1040.line24 refuse on gate refund.box8; with no, s1.line1 $1,400.00). The opposite error, a business-only tax answered NO, is not invited: the question names the kind of tax and gives box 8 as the example. Safe; adding 'not a tax of general application' would sharpen it (optional).

A business-only income tax refund never deducted is refused although the tool's zero would be right (f1099g p. 5: 'If taxable, report the amount in box 2 on Schedule C or F'). Refusal is safe; same disposition as group 3 finding 1.

unruled:f8962.alloc.reason: No defect. One WIDE: a policy member in no tax family is 'not in' the filer's tax family and draws Yes though no Part IV allocation applies; f8962.other also refuses APTC for someone in no one's tax family. Safe.

findings.evidence: i8962 pp. 12, 17: allocation is for 'at least one individual in another tax family'; a member in no tax family draws Yes here, and f8962.other ('advance payments were made for someone who is in no one's tax family') refuses the same lines anyway. Safe.

unruled:f8962.other.reason: No defect. Four WIDE and one UNCLEAR that leans WIDE: each reading that matters gives Yes and refuses f8962.line24 and line25; no reading lets an unsupported case compute.

findings.evidence: i8962 p. 4: MEC eligibility of a tax family member not enrolled in a Marketplace plan does not change the coverage family; 'anyone in your tax family' refuses. Safe.
i8962 p. 6: a Marketplace determination of Medicaid/CHIP ineligibility on accurate information is not MEC eligibility; the question's Medicaid item refuses it. Safe.
i8962 p. 5: an offer treated as unaffordable after an accurate APTC determination draws Yes on the 9.02% test. Safe.
i8962 p. 3: an unaffordable individual coverage HRA with reimbursements opted out draws Yes on 'offered'. Safe.
i8962 p. 3: mid-month eligibility for other MEC read as 'for any month' gives Yes and refuses; under the every-day rule No is also right. Safe; as before.

unruled:f8962.premium_adjust.reason: No defect. The unpaid-premium NARROW is covered by f8962.other, which asks whether any part of a month's premium was not paid by the due date and gates f8962.line24 and line25 (BUG-0327 closed by ptc-sa PENDING-3); the refund UNCLEAR leans WIDE.

findings.evidence: i8962 p. 4: a month's premium unpaid by the unextended due date. f8962.other asks 'any part of a month's premium was not paid by the due date of your return, not including extensions' and refuses f8962.line24 and f8962.line25, the lines this screen gates. BUG-0327's unpaid-share part, closed by ptc-sa PENDING-3.

i8962 p. 4: column A reports enrollment premiums, net of 2025 refunds. A filer whose refund is already reflected in column A answers Yes and is refused though column A as reported is right; any refund draws Yes, so no reading lets an unreflected refund compute. Safe.

unruled:sa.dependent.reason: No defect: the parenthetical is the Form 1040 dependent-question carve-out, not an EIC import. i1040gi pp. 18–19, Step 4/5: "If the person who could claim you on their 2025 tax return is not required to file, and isn’t filing a 2025 tax return or is filing a 2025 return only to claim a refund of withheld income tax or estimated tax paid, check ‘No.’" The reviewer's pages (34–35, 41–42) do not include pp. 18–19. The line 12a checkbox and the Standard Deduction Worksheet for Dependents use that answer, so a filer in the carve-out is not claimable for this purpose and the full standard deduction is right.
